% Problem Set 6 -- 9 problems. (Q2 is identical to PS5 Q7.)
% Do not edit except to fix statement typos.
\problemset{6}{}

\problem{6}{1}{Let $p\colon X\onto Y$ be a closed continuous surjective map such that
$p^{-1}(y)$ is compact for each $y\in Y$. Prove that if $Y$ is compact, then so is $X$.}

\problem{6}{2}{Let $X$ be a compact metric space. Prove that if $f\colon X\to X$ is an
isometry (distance preserving map) of $X$, then $f$ is a homeomorphism.}

\problem{6}{3}{Prove that the composition of two quotient maps is a quotient map.}

\problem{6}{4}{Prove that a surjective continuous map $f\colon X\onto Y$ that is either an
open map or a closed map is a quotient map.}

\problem{6}{5}{Prove that a bijective quotient map is a homeomorphism.}

\problem{6}{6}{Let $f_1\colon X_1\to Y_1$ and $f_2\colon X_2\to Y_2$ be maps between
topological spaces, and let $f_1\times f_2\colon X_1\times X_2\to Y_1\times Y_2$ denote the
product map $(x_1,x_2)\mapsto(f_1(x_1),f_2(x_2))$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
  \item Prove that if $f_1$ and $f_2$ are continuous, then $f_1\times f_2$ is continuous with
        respect to the product topologies.
  \item Give a counterexample to show that if $p_1\colon X_1\to Y_1$ and
        $p_2\colon X_2\to Y_2$ are quotient maps, $p_1\times p_2$ need not be a quotient map.
\end{enumerate}}

\problem{6}{7}{Let $X$ and $Y$ be topological spaces, and $f\colon X\to Y$ be a bijective
continuous map. Show that if $Y$ is Hausdorff, then $X$ is also Hausdorff.}

\problem{6}{8}{Let $X$ be a compact topological space and $p\colon X\onto Y$ be a quotient
map.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
  \item Prove that $Y$ is compact.
  \item Show that if $Y$ is Hausdorff, then $p$ is a closed map.
\end{enumerate}}

\problem{6}{9}{Let $p\colon X\to Y$ be a continuous surjection. Prove that $p$ is a closed
map if and only if for every subset $S\subseteq Y$ and every open set $U\subseteq X$
containing $p^{-1}(S)$, there exists an open set $V\subseteq Y$ containing $S$ such that
$p^{-1}(V)\subseteq U$.}
